description: Weekly plan for ages thirteen to eighteen: prayer from conviction, respectful disagreement, study and the future, screens, sleep, worry and siblings.

topics.focus: Prayer from conviction: dialogue, not orders

actions.text: Ask calmly about their relationship with prayer, and listen without blame or interruption.
Pray one prayer with them at the mosque or at home this week, and make it your time together.
Share honestly something prayer gives you, without a long sermon.
If they have questions about faith, don't get angry; look for the answer together from a trusted source.
Agree to pause a heated argument until you are both calm, then come back to it.
Hear their whole point of view before replying, and say it back so they know you understood.
Avoid insults and sarcasm during a disagreement, and apologise if you get it wrong.
Give them a real decision about something of theirs this week, within clear limits.

topics.focus: Study and the future: a clear goal

actions.text: Sit with them to make a realistic weekly study plan that they write themselves.
Ask which subject is hardest and look for the right help together.
Talk about a long-term goal they care about and link one small step to it this week.
Praise discipline and effort, and avoid comparing them with their peers.

topics.focus: Screen balance with trust and responsibility

actions.text: Agree together on phone limits: bedtime, study time and meals.
Ask what they follow online out of curiosity, not as an interrogation.
Lead by example: put your own phone away at meals and family conversations.
Suggest one screen-free activity together this week: sport, a walk or volunteering.

topics.focus: Enough sleep in the teenage years

actions.text: Agree on a time for devices off at night, with the phone charging outside the bedroom.
Encourage a wake-up time that stays the same, or close to it, every day.
Talk with them about how late nights affect mood and focus, without lecturing.
Cut back on stimulants such as coffee and energy drinks in the evening.

topics.focus: Worry and pressure: you're not alone

actions.text: Set a weekly phone-free time to talk, and ask what is on their mind.
Accept their feelings without brushing them off: "It sounds like this is weighing on you."
Help them break a big problem into small steps.
If you notice sadness or withdrawal lasting two weeks or more, consult a specialist.

topics.focus: Sibling relationships in the teenage years

actions.text: Respect their privacy in front of their siblings, and don't criticise them in front of the others.
Give them a lead role with younger siblings on a specific task, and praise how they handle it.
Avoid comparing them with their siblings on school or behaviour.
Make some one-to-one time with them, away from their siblings, this week.

worship.text: Pray one prayer together at home every day this week.
Ask your teenager to choose a volunteering activity you all take part in.
Sit together once this week to read the tafsir of a verse they choose, from a trusted tafsir book.
Read two pages of the Qur'an together on Friday.
Make du'a together for each family member by name after one of the prayers this week.
Give charity together and let them choose where it goes.
